title: Handoff Pocket Journal — Night Ops Notebook (2026-10-21)
content:
Night pocket journal — quick handoff notes and follow-ups (informal)

High-level summary:
- Quiet night overall but noticed recurring small latency spikes on hosted-api model route 'gpt-open-16k' between 02:10–03:05 PDT. No user-visible errors or increase in 5xx, but p95 token latency rose ~30% for short prompts (~<150 tokens).
- Root suspicion: transient KV-cache misses coincident with small background rollout/garbage-collection job triggered by allocator-controller on dedicated pools.
- Mitigation: temporarily bumped route preference to lower-cost but warmer pool (policy bump done by Ethan at 03:22 PDT) which normalized p95 back to baseline.

What I observed / timeline (timestamps PDT):
- 01:58 — handoff from day crew, no open incidents. noted increased queue depth on batcher-3 in metrics but within target.
- 02:12 — first small spike in p95 observed on dashboards (Console -> Per-route -> gpt-open-16k). Alert threshold did not fire (set conservatively).
- 02:14 — checked autoscaler logs: short flurry of container restarts for pool-ded-A (approx 3 resched events). logs in github PR above show similar restarts during integration test earlier today.
- 02:20 — traced requests in distributed tracing; several requests had KV-cache miss ratios jump from 2% -> 18% for a 15min window.
- 02:40 — internal note: no 5xx, error budget safe, but latency SLO inching toward soft boundary.
- 03:05 — batcher queue flushed, KV cache warmed back up on most nodes. p95 trending down.
- 03:22 — manual route preference bump to warmer pool applied as temporary mitigation. p95 stable by 03:30.

Immediate actions taken (by shift):
- Quick runbook checks: confirmed kv-cache-runbook steps (Confluence) and validated cache-health metrics (sentry: cache_hit_ratio, cache_miss_ratio).
- Escalation: Not escalated to oncall+1 since no user impact and error budget not breached. Ethan looped in because he owns pool-ded-A config.
- Mitigation: applied route preference override (short TTL) to shift traffic to pool-ded-B while we observe.

Runbook deltas / notes to formalize:
- kv-cache-runbook currently assumes cold-start only after full node recycle. Observed partial warm->cold behaviour when allocator-controller triggered small GC. Add step: check allocator-controller GC windows and correlate with container restarts.
- Add a short checklist item: when p95 spike observed without 5xx, verify cache_miss_ratio and container restart count before paging oncall+1. This could avoid noisy pages.
- Recommended metric add: track "route-pref-switches" as an event metric to correlate manual preference changes with latency regressions.

Follow-ups / Action items (owners):
- Ethan Cole: investigate allocator-controller GC config for pool-ded-A and open a change proposal if pattern repeats (JIRA-SRE-4271). Target: post-mortem decision tree by 2026-10-28.
- Priya Desai: add checklist item to kv-cache-runbook + add metric pipeline for route-pref-switches (Confluence page + PR to monitored-metrics repo). Target: 2026-10-25.
- Ava Martinez (me): draft a short internal note for customers/stakeholders if we see recurrence; keep this doc as running log. Also add a small Grafana panel linking cache_miss_ratio, restart_count, and p95 for quick triage. Target: 2026-10-24.

Open questions / things I couldn't confirm tonight:
- Were there any low-priority orchestrator jobs (scheduled) that align with the 02:10 window? I saw a job in the scheduler logs but couldn't confirm whether it induced GC. Need platform infra to validate.
- Is the allocator-controller telemetry sampling rate sufficient? current sampling looks sparse for short spikes.

Quick triage checklist I used (keep for next handoff):
- Confirm no 5xx spike and error budget OK.
- Check per-route p50/p95/p99 for the last 1h and last 24h.
- Verify cache_miss_ratio and recent node restart counts.
- Look at autoscaler events and allocator-controller logs.
- If cache misses > 10% and restarts > 2 in 10m: consider temporary route-pref bump. Else: wait and monitor.

Short-term notes to next shift (pull-forward items):
- If you see recurrence within 48h escalate to oncall+1. This doc will be updated with exact escalation thresholds after Ethan's investigation.
- If route-pref-bump is used, ensure TTL set to 30m and document in 'route-change-log' (PR template exists in infra repo).

Random observations / notes to self (informal):
- Seeing small noise in batcher-3 metrics more often than before lunch. Could be correlated with background cleanup in model shards.
- I left a pinned Slack thread in #sre-night-ops with the most useful span traces.

References and quick links (for on-call):
- KV cache runbook: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SRE/kv-cache-runbook
- Related PR (restart behavior test): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/812
- Jira ticket for follow-up: JIRA-SRE-4271

Signing off (03:55 PDT) — handoff to morning crew: Liam O'Connor (on at 07:00).

-- Ava

[Notes: informal, keep in Drive as working log. Will trim and move to confluence if post-mortem needed.]
